claims.text: AlCrFeNiSi is a high-entropy alloy.
The AlCrFeNiSi feedstock is cobalt-free.
A controlled powder-bed or build-platform preheating step should be introduced during additive manufacturing.
The intervention is intended for laser powder bed fusion with a preheat temperature on the order of several hundred degrees Celsius.
Powder-bed preheating reduces thermal gradients during solidification.
Reduced thermal gradients promote a more chemically homogeneous microstructure with less compositional segregation.
Reduced thermal gradients lower the concentrations of microcracks and void defects.
Preheating decreases differential cooling rates and thermal-contraction mismatches.
Preheating slows phase separation.
Preheating reduces residual stresses generated by rapid cooling.
Preheating suppresses defect nucleation during layer-wise deposition.
Lower segregation, residual stress, and defect nucleation improve the mechanical integrity of the final component.
Preheated AlCrFeNiSi samples will have lower residual stress than conventionally fabricated or unpreheated samples.
Preheated AlCrFeNiSi samples will have finer and more uniform microstructural features with reduced segregation.
Preheated AlCrFeNiSi samples will contain fewer internal defects.
Preheated AlCrFeNiSi samples will exhibit enhanced mechanical strength and integrity.
The proposed effect is limited to comparable alloy compositions, atmospheres, and laser-processing conditions.
Preheat-induced phase transformations could invalidate the proposed benefit.
The optimal preheat temperature and the magnitudes of the effects on segregation, residual stress, defects, and mechanical properties are not yet quantified.
Failure to obtain statistically significant reductions in residual stress, segregation, and defect density together with improved mechanical integrity would falsify the hypothesis.
